Would that they themselves, and those who offer and beg us for peace, and yet declare and wage war on us over the sacramentarian matter, would at least consider this: that they have never been able to obtain anything by it; and that, by separating themselves from their fellow servants, they do the most welcome thing for Antichrist, moved to join arms with us against Antichrist? Would that they preferred to stand with us in the same battle line rather than to stir up sedition among the domestics of the faith and fellow soldiers (who, by the grace of Christ, are certainly not inferior in the gifts of the Holy Spirit, in the equipment of spiritual weapons, or in readiness for the defence of the gospel). Would that they might learn to magnify and love Christ in his members. We, indeed, being well aware of our own good conscience, both because the truth stands on our side and because for the sake of the Church we have often offered peace to them, do not doubt that God will always bless our holy cause.

units.la: III. Iitueatur[?] etiam ingeniosa & pia Iuuentus, magnorum & illustrium Ecclesiae Doctorum & luminum exempla, quae testantur eos vbi sese graui-ter errauisse animaduertissent, sententiam in melius mutauisse. Eusebius historiae Ecclesiasticae auctor, ante Nicenam Synodum Ariana haeresi imbutus fuit; sed erroris onustus, eundem pie abiecit: ac sunt qui Symbolum Nicenum ab eodem conscriptum esse, perhibeant. Augustinus initio Manichaeus fuit, ac religioe[?] matri Monicae diuturni & ingentis lu-ctus autor extitit. Sed hanc consolatus est Ambrosius, Mediolanensis Episcopus, dicens: Filius tot tantarum-que lacrymarum perire non potest. Ac tanta fuit Augustini senis virtus, tantum veritatis studiū, ut iam olim Orthodoxam amplexus religionem, senex Retractationum libros scripserit, commemora-bili sane studij erga veritatem & modestiae exemplo. Ac profecto digna est memoria haec illius sententia: Non errare, Angelicum est[?]: errorem defendere, diabol-cum.
units.tr: III. Let the ingenious and pious youth also look at the examples of great and illustrious teachers and lights of the Church, who bear witness that when they perceived they had gravely erred, they changed their opinion for the better. Eusebius, the author of the Ecclesiastical History, was imbued with the Arian heresy before the Synod of Nicaea; but, burdened with his error, he piously cast it off; and there are those who report that the Nicene Creed was written by him. Augustine was at first a Manichaean, and was the cause of long and great grief to his mother Monica. But Ambrose, Bishop of Milan, consoled her, saying: "The son of so many and such great tears cannot perish." And so great was the virtue of the aged Augustine, and so great his zeal for truth, that, having long before embraced the orthodox religion, he wrote in old age the books of his Retractations, a memorable example indeed of zeal for truth and of modesty. And truly that saying of his is worthy of remembrance: "Not to err is angelic; to defend error is diabolical."

units.la: Philippus Melanchthon, lecto, Doctoris ortho-doxi & pij, D. Oecolampadij, celeberrimę Basiliensis Ecclesiae vigilantissimi Antistitis, Dialogo de Eucharistia, locū dedit nostrae doctrinae, quam esse vera tum animaduertit: & postea cū nostrarum Ecclesiarū doctoribus & pastoribus, constanter vsq; ad extremum vitae spiritum pacem, sanctè coluit. Horum optimorum virorum exemplis juventutem commoveri aequū est, sic ut eos non audiat, qui, ut Augustini verbis vtar, Nimis perverse seipsos amat, & ideo alios errare volunt, ut ipsorum errores lateant: qui sectae alicuius Androclidas agunt, & sibi pedaneos suffragatores quaerunt & conciliant; nec tamen hos alite tractant, quàm olim Dionysius tyrannus suos parastos[?], quos Saliuam ipsius lingere, & nectaris habere ƀco[?], necesse erat.
units.tr: Philip Melanchthon, having read the dialogue on the Eucharist of the learned, orthodox and pious teacher Dr Oecolampadius, most vigilant bishop of the most celebrated Church of Basel, gave a place to our doctrine, which he noticed to be true; and afterwards, together with the teachers and ministers of our churches, he faithfully cultivated peace, constantly, to the last breath of his life. It is fitting that the youth be moved by the examples of these most excellent men, so as not to listen to those who, to use the words of Augustine, love themselves too perversely, and therefore wish others to err so that their own errors may lie hidden: who play the Androclides for some sect and seek and win for themselves footstool supporters; nor do they treat these men otherwise than Dionysius the tyrant once treated his parasites, whom it was necessary to lick his spittle and to have nectar [?].

units.la: IIII. Semper autem intueantur omnium ordinum & aetatum homines, Iesu Christi Domini nostri, qui Veritas & Sapientia nostra est, exemplum; ac saepe repetant illustre dictum Ignatii: ἐμοὶ ἀρχεῖα ὁ Χριστός, οὗ [illegible, ~6 letters] πρόσπαλαι ἀληθής. Mihi venerandae antiquitatis instar est Christus, cui non dicto obtemperantem esse, manifestum est exitium[?]. Et illud beati Martyris Cypriani: Non quoic[?] aut ille ante nos dixerint, esse attendendum, sed quid dixit Christus, qui ante omnes est. Christum Iesum itaque audiamus, amemus, spiremus, imitemur, celebremus, & in ipso in sempiternum unum esse exoptemus.
units.tr: IV. Let men of every rank and age always look to the example of Jesus Christ our Lord, who is our Truth and our Wisdom; and let them often repeat the famous saying of Ignatius: "Christ is to me the archive, the unshaken and ancient truth." "To me Christ is in the place of venerable antiquity; to obey whom in every word is manifestly..." [remainder illegible]. And that of the blessed martyr Cyprian: "It is not to be heeded what someone of those before us has said, but what Christ, who is before all, has said." Let us therefore hear Christ Jesus, love him, breathe him, imitate him, celebrate him, and desire to be one with him in him for ever.

units.tr: The proud have mocked me greatly; yet I have not turned aside from your teaching.

units.la: Irrideri ab improbis, laudari est.
units.tr: To be mocked by the wicked is to be praised.

units.la: Non ego dura pati discrimina mille recuso, Dum tua constanti ueor mandata labore. Sed ne deficiam, ne sæuo vincar ab hoste, Tu mihi præstò veni, tu suffice robora fesso.
units.tr: I do not refuse to bear a thousand dangers, while I keep your commandments with steadfast labour. But lest I fail, lest I be conquered by the cruel enemy, come to me at once; give strength to me, weary as I am.
